ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p150/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p150/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p150/r1.claim: The Moses and Pharaoh story fits the sūrah’s theme: Moses earnestly called Pharaoh from arrogance, and God destroyed the resistant tyrant with a slight onslaught of wind.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p150/r1.anchor: Moses (sws) very earnestly tried to bring the Pharaoh to the right path

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p162/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p162/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p162/r4.claim: The Moses account primarily addresses Quraysh: the wise learn from others' fate instead of waiting for calamity to strike them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p162/r4.anchor: they should learn a lesson from this tale

BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.claim: The surah’s purpose is to establish resurrection and the gathering, displaying humanity’s final fate after the preceding surahs’ full exposition; its oaths show the matter has reached its decisive climax.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433#2/r8.claim: Pharaoh's fate is an instructive warning and a threat to the unbelievers addressed through Muhammad.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433#2/r8.anchor: ثم وقف تعالى على موضع العبرة بحال فرعون وتعذيبه، وفي الكلام وعيد للكفار المخاطبين برسالة محمد

STUDYQURAN:79:intro/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:intro/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:79:intro/r7.claim: The Moses and Pharaoh account is likely the earliest revealed account of them and likens Pharaoh's disbelief to that of Makkan idolaters.
STUDYQURAN:79:intro/r7.anchor: most likely the first account of the story of Moses and Pharaoh in the chronological order of revelation

TABATABAI:79:27-34/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:27-34/r1.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:79:27-34/r1.claim: One reported reading supplies an omitted object: the warning is a lesson for whoever fears God; the author says the preceding interpretation is more eloquent.
TABATABAI:79:27-34/r1.anchor: وقيل المفعول محذوف والتقدير لمن يخشى الله والوجه السابق أبلغ

ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r31.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r31.speaker: author
ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r31.claim: The story and punishment teach a lesson especially to those capable of reverent fear, who possess understanding.
ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r31.anchor: Fakat herkes için değil لِّمَن{ }يَخْشَىٰٓ haşyet duymak şânından olan, saygısı bulunan kimseler için ki onlar irfânı olanlardır.

ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r32.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r32.speaker: author
ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r32.claim: The spiritually insensitive gain nothing from Moses' coming and Pharaoh's drowning; the news of resurrection works the same way.
ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r32.anchor: Yoksa duygusu olmayanlar bir Mûsâ gelmiş, Firavun batmış da ne olmuş diye bundan hiçbir istifade etmezler. İşte o ba‘s hakkındaki haber de böyledir.

QASHANI:79:18-26/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:79:18-26/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:79:18-26/r7.claim: Pharaoh’s punishment is a lesson for the one who fears: the soul should humble, soften, and break so it no longer makes claims.
QASHANI:79:18-26/r7.anchor: ويروى: قصمته، وذلك القهر هو معنى قوله: { فأخذه الله نكال الآخرة والأولى * إن في ذلك لعبرة لمن يخشى }

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p329/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p329/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p329/r7.claim: The punishment of Pharaoh is a lesson for whoever fears God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p329/r7.anchor: إن في ذلك} الذي فعل بفرعون حين كذب وعصى {لعبرة} لعظة {لمن يخشى} الله عز وجل.

BAYDAWI-FULL:79:24-26/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:24-26/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:24-26/r7.claim: The event is a lesson for anyone disposed to fear.
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:24-26/r7.anchor: { إن فى ذلك لعبرة لمن يخشى } لمن كان من شأنه الخشية

BINTSHATI:v1p149/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p149/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p149/r6.claim: Possible lexical origins of ʿibra include weighing coins to assess their value, crossing a valley, reading a text reflectively, and a well-traveled camel.
BINTSHATI:v1p149/r6.anchor: وربما كان استعماله اللغوي الأول في تعبير الدراهمأي وزنها لمعرفة قيمتها، أو من: عبر الوادي. إذا قطعه من عبره إلى عبره.

BINTSHATI:v1p149/r7.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p149/r7.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p149/r7.claim: Taking a lesson means seeing an example, weighing and considering it, and being admonished; Pharaoh’s fate is the example for anyone who fears.
BINTSHATI:v1p149/r7.anchor: واستعمال العبرة في الاعتبار، ملحوظ فيه أن المرء يرى مثلاً أمامه فيزنه ويخبره ويتدبره ويتعظ به.

JISHUMI:v10p7268/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7268/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7268/r8.claim: Khashya and khawf mean the same thing: fear.
JISHUMI:v10p7268/r8.anchor: والخشية والخوف بمعنى، خشي يخشى خشية

JISHUMI:v10p7268/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7268/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7268/r12.claim: ʿIbra is a sign by which truth is grasped, from the idea of crossing over to truth; the root also appears in crossing a river and interpreting a dream.
JISHUMI:v10p7268/r12.anchor: والعبرة: الدلالة التي يدرك بها الحق، وأصله من العبور، كأنه عبر به إلى الحق

JISHUMI:v10p7271/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7271/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7271/r4.claim: The event is an admonition for whoever fears God's punishment and vengeance.
JISHUMI:v10p7271/r4.anchor: إن في ذلك لعبرة لعظة لمن يخشى عقاب الله تعالى، ونقمته

JISHUMI:v10p7271/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7271/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7271/r9.claim: The verse makes reflection on proofs and examples obligatory; those who fear are singled out because they benefit from it.
JISHUMI:v10p7271/r9.anchor: ويدل قوله: (إن في ذلك لعبرة) على وجوب التدبر في الأدلة والأمثال، وخص من يخشى؛ لأنهم ينتفعون به

MUQATIL:79:15-26/r16.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:79:15-26/r16.speaker: author
MUQATIL:79:15-26/r16.claim: Pharaoh and his people were destroyed as a lesson for those who fear and remember God's punishment, so they avoid associating partners with Him.
MUQATIL:79:15-26/r16.anchor: يقول: لمن يخشى عقوبة الله تعالى، مثل ما فعل آل فرعون فلا يشرك،

MUQATIL:79:15-26/r17.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:79:15-26/r17.speaker: author
MUQATIL:79:15-26/r17.claim: The warning addresses Meccan disbelievers: if they deny Muhammad, they may suffer the punishment that befell Pharaoh's people.
MUQATIL:79:15-26/r17.anchor: يخوف كفار مكة لئلا يكذبوا محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم فيجازيهم مثل ما حل بقوم فرعون من العذاب.

NAHHAS:v5p143/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p143/r16.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p143/r16.claim: One should fear God's punishment as it came upon others when they disobeyed.
NAHHAS:v5p143/r16.anchor: أي يخشى عقاب الله كما نزل بغيره لما عصى

QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r25.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r25.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r25.claim: Pharaoh's fate is a lesson and admonition for anyone who fears God.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:22-26/r25.anchor: { إن في ذلك لعبرة } أي اعتبارا وعظة. { لمن يخشى } أي يخاف الله عز وجل.

TABATABAI:79:23-26/r16.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:23-26/r16.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:23-26/r16.claim: The story of Moses is an admonition for anyone disposed by sound human nature to fear misery and punishment; the object of fear is left unstated.
TABATABAI:79:23-26/r16.anchor: الظاهر أن مفعول { يخشى } منسي معرض عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p31/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p31/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p31/r1.claim: ‘That’ means the account of Pharaoh, what he did, and what was done to him; it provides a great lesson.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p31/r1.anchor: إن في ذلك أي فيما ذكر من قصة فرعون وما فعل وما فعل به لعبرة عظيمة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p31/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p31/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p31/r2.claim: The lesson is for one disposed to fear and capable of knowledge; one explanation is that someone already fearing needs no further lesson, while another includes both present fear and the capacity for it.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p31/r2.anchor: أي لمن شأنه أن يخشى وهو من من شأنه المعرفة وهذا إما لأن من كان في خشية

BINTSHATI:v1p142/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p142/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p142/r2.claim: The Qur'an presents a tyrant's fate as an admonition for whoever fears.
BINTSHATI:v1p142/r2.anchor: وبحسب القرآن أن يلفت إلى مصير طاغية، ليكون عبرة لمن يخشى

BINTSHATI:v1p142/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p142/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p142/r3.claim: The account omits Moses' upbringing, his first relations with Pharaoh, the date, the great sign, and the precise punishment because these details are not the essential lesson.
BINTSHATI:v1p142/r3.anchor: لم يذكر نشأة موسى، وصلته الأولى بفرعون. ولم يحدد تاريخ الحادثة

BINTSHATI:v1p142/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p142/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p142/r4.claim: The arresting question begins the account at Moses' call in the holy valley, folding away what preceded it; the parallel account in Taha begins with Moses seeing a fire.
BINTSHATI:v1p142/r4.anchor: فطوى كل ما كان من قصة موسى قبل هذا الحديث إذ ناداه ربه بالوادي المقدس طوى

BIQAI-FULL:v8p317/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p317/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p317/r1.claim: Pharaoh is a byword for evil and filth, and all sects agree on cursing him.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p317/r1.anchor: فرعون الذي أجمع على لعنه جميع الطوائف . وهو مثل عندهم في الشرارة والخبث

BIQAI-FULL:v8p317/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p317/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p317/r2.claim: The concise retelling avoids contradiction, initially introduces the story accessibly, and in the sūra’s arrangement recalls the fuller account for the audience.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p317/r2.anchor: وأما من جهة الترتيب فلتذكيرهم بما مضى ليجتمع في المخيلة في أقرب وقت ويتذكر به ذلك المبسوط

BIQAI-FULL:v8p317/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p317/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p317/r3.claim: A lesson is a deliberate passage from one meaning to another that leads to knowledge; fear of God is the foundation of good.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p317/r3.anchor: أمرا عظيما يتعمد الاعتبار به من معنى إلى معنى حتى يقع به الوصول إلى كثير من المعارف

BIQAI-FULL:v8p317/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p317/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p317/r4.claim: The listener should move from the Israelites’ rescue despite weakness to Pharaoh’s defeat, the sea’s splitting and drowning, and other signs as lessons in punishment and resurrection.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p317/r4.anchor: فأول العبور أن ينقل السامع حال غيره إليه فيتذكر بإنجاء بني إسرائيل على ضعفهم منهم على قوتهم ثم بقوة ما حصل لهم من القهر

BIQAI-FULL:v8p317/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p317/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p317/r5.claim: The signs in Pharaoh’s story show God’s power to punish disbelievers and tyrants, and especially to bring about resurrection.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p317/r5.anchor: قدرة الله تعالى على إيراد الكفار النار وقهر كل جبار

BIQAI-FULL:v8p317/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p317/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p317/r6.claim: Pharaoh’s story culminates in proof of God’s total power, especially resurrection; denial of resurrection gathers evil, while belief gathers good, leading into the creation argument.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p317/r6.anchor: وكان أعظم عبرتها القدرة التامة لا سيما على البعث كما هي مشيرة إليه بأولها وآخرها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p22/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p22/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p22/r1.claim: What happened to Pharaoh is a lesson and warning for anyone who fears God.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p22/r1.anchor: إن في ذلك الذي فعل بفرعون لعبرة أي لعظة لمن يخشى الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p315/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p315/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p315/r1.claim: Moses’ story warns Muhammad that opponents who deny his message will meet Pharaoh’s fate.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p315/r1.anchor: وكذلك عاقبة من خالفك وكذب بما جئت به؛ ولهذا قال في آخر القصة: {إن في ذلك لعبرة لمن يخشى}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p315#3/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p315#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p315#3/r1.claim: The story is a lesson for anyone who takes admonition and is warned.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p315#3/r1.anchor: وقوله: {إن في ذلك لعبرة لمن يخشى} أي: لمن يتعظ وينزجر.

JISHUMI:v10p7263/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7263/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7263/r3.claim: One view makes إن في ذلك لعبرة the explicit answer to the oath.
JISHUMI:v10p7263/r3.anchor: ثم اتصل به صفة البعث، ووقته. وقيل: بل جوابه مذكور، ثم اختلفوا فقيل: جوابه (إن في ذلك لعبرة)،

JISHUMI:v10p7263/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7263/r6.speaker: أبي بن خلف
JISHUMI:v10p7263/r6.claim: Ubayy b. Khalaf challenged resurrection with a decayed bone; after the Prophet affirmed return and punishment, Ubayy derided it as a losing return, and the passage was revealed.
JISHUMI:v10p7263/r6.anchor: روي أن أبي بن خلف أخذ عظما باليا، وقال: أتعدنا يا محمد، وقد صرنا هكذا أنا لمردودون خلقا جديدا؟

NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#4/r1.claim: The events just mentioned are a lesson for whoever fears Allah.

BURSEVI:v10p251/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p251/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p251/r12.claim: That refers to Pharaoh’s story and what God did to him.
BURSEVI:v10p251/r12.anchor: أي فيما ذكر من قصة فرعون وما فعل به

BURSEVI:v10p251/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p251/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p251/r13.claim: The one disposed to fear is one with knowledge: a knower of God and His attributes fears Him and does not rebel against God or His messengers lest punishment descend.
BURSEVI:v10p251/r13.anchor: إن العارف بالله وبشؤونه يخشى منه فلا يتمرد على الله ولا على أنبيائه

BURSEVI:v10p251/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p251/r14.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p251/r14.claim: A wise person learns from another’s fate rather than waiting to suffer the same consequence.

RAZI-FULL:v31p40#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p40#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p40#3/r1.claim: The story of Moses and Pharaoh, Pharaoh’s humiliation, and Moses’ triumph warn the God-fearing to abandon rebellion and denial lest they suffer the same punishment.
RAZI-FULL:v31p40#3/r1.anchor: فيما اقتصصناه من أمر موسى وفرعون ، وما أحله الله بفرعون من الخزي

RAZI-FULL:v31p40#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p40#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p40#3/r2.claim: The deniers of Muhammad should infer that sharing Pharaoh’s culpable conduct will bring them the same punishment; God supports His prophets and messengers.
RAZI-FULL:v31p40#3/r2.anchor: فاعتبروا معاشر المكذبين لمحمد بما ذكرناه ، أي اعلموا أنكم إن شاركتموهم

TAB-FULL:v24p88/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p88/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p88/r1.claim: God's seizure and worldly punishment of Pharaoh are a lesson for whoever fears God and His punishment.
TAB-FULL:v24p88/r1.anchor: نكل به فجعل {نكال الآخرة} [النازعات: 25] مصدرا من معناه

TAB-FULL:v24p88/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p88/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p88/r2.claim: Nakal is an accusative verbal noun derived in meaning from “God seized him” rather than from the same root or wording.
TAB-FULL:v24p88/r2.anchor: نكل به فجعل {نكال الآخرة} [النازعات: 25] مصدرا من معناه، لا من لفظه

THALABI:v10p127/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p127/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p127/r7.claim: Pharaoh's fate is a lesson for whoever fears.
THALABI:v10p127/r7.anchor: إن في ذلك لعبرة لمن يخشى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p191/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p191/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p191/r1.claim: The event involving Pharaoh, who disbelieved and disobeyed, is a lesson and admonition for whoever fears God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p191/r1.anchor: {إن في ذلك} الذي فعل (¬5) فرعون حين كذب، وعصى. {لعبرة} يريد فكرة، وعظة. {لمن يخشى} الله.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p191/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p191/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p191/r2.claim: After the lesson from Pharaoh, the discourse turns to address those who deny resurrection.

BURHAN:v3p192/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p192/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p192/r1.claim: One view places the oath's answer at “a lesson for whoever fears”; in the magicians' “we will never prefer you,” an omitted element is recoverable from the preceding speech.

TABRISI:79:25-26/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:79:25-26/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:79:25-26/r7.claim: Pharaoh’s fate is a lesson and evidence for anyone who fears God and His punishment, enabling the discerning to distinguish truth from falsehood.
TABRISI:79:25-26/r7.anchor: الله تعالى ويخاف عقابه ونقمته ودلالة يمكن أن يعتبر بها العاقل

TABRISI:79:25-26/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:79:25-26/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:79:25-26/r8.claim: The account of Moses follows mention of those who denied prophets and resurrection, consoling Muhammad, urging patience after Moses, warning his people, and reinforcing the proof.
TABRISI:79:25-26/r8.anchor: وجه اتصال قصة موسى ع بما قبلها أنه لما تقدم ذكر المكذبين للأنبياء المنكرين للبعث

QUSHAYRI:v3p389/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p389/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p389/r9.claim: Pharaoh's destruction is a lesson for anyone who fears God.
QUSHAYRI:v3p389/r9.anchor: أي في إهلاكنا فرعون لعبرة لمن يخشى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r13.claim: Pharaoh’s fate warns those who fear God’s punishment in this world and the next.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r13.anchor: إن في ذلك: فيما جرى لفرعون وأخذه تلك الأخذة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p81/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p81/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p81/r8.claim: The story’s concluding summary explains the content of the earlier introduction, ‘Have Moses’ story come to you?’
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p81/r8.anchor: وجاء في آخر القصة بحوصلة وفذلكة لما تقدم فقال : { إن في ذلك لعبرة لمن يخشى } فهو في معنى البيان لمضمون جملة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p81/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p81/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p81/r9.claim: ‘That’ points to the account of Moses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p81/r9.anchor: والإشارة بقوله : { في ذلك } إلى { حديث موسى } ( النازعات : 15 ) .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p81/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p81/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p81/r10.claim: An ʿibra is a state from which the mind moves to know its outcome and the outcomes of analogous cases.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p81/r10.anchor: والعبرة : الحالة التي ينتقل الذهن من معرفتها إلى معرفة عاقبتها وعاقبة أمثالها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p81/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p81/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p81/r11.claim: The word ʿibra derives from crossing from one bank of a valley or river to the other.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p81/r11.anchor: وهي مشتقة من العبر ، وهو الانتقال من ضفة واد أو نهر إلى ضفته الأخرى .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p81/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p81/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p81/r13.claim: The indefinite ʿibra magnifies the many lessons about deeds and outcomes, vigilance and fear of God, and the consequences of virtue and its opposite in this life and the next.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p81/r13.anchor: وتنوين ( عبرة ) للتعظيم لأن في هذه القصة مواعظ كثيرة من جهات هي مثلات للأعمال وعواقبها ، ومراقبة الله وخشيته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p81/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p81/r14.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p81/r14.claim: Those who fear God are people of knowledge who infer implications and hidden consequences; Ibn ʿĀshūr links this to verses on learned fear, understanding parables, and Moses’ call to fear God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p81/r14.anchor: لأن الذين يخشون الله هم أهل المعرفة الذين يفهمون دلالة الأشياء على لوازمها وخفاياها ، قال تعالى
